pills.text: OPTIONAL ADVANCED ENRICHMENT
INDIA'S STRUGGLE FOR INDEPENDENCE PRESENTS THE NO-CHANGER VERSUS PRO-CHANGER
A DISAGREEMENT OVER METHOD AFTER THE SUSPENSION OF MASS
NO-CHANGERS DEFENDED GANDHIAN CONSTRUCTIVE WORK AS PREPARATION FOR FUTURE
SWARAJISTS ARGUED THAT ENTERING LEGISLATURES WOULD PREVENT POLITICAL PASSIVITY
THEIR 1923 SUCCESSES GAVE THEM A PLATFORM, BUT OBSTRUCTION
DAS'S DEATH IN 1925 WEAKENED LEADERSHIP.
THE HRA AIMED AT AN ARMED OVERTHROW OF COLONIAL

groups.heading: OPTIONAL SOURCE DEPTH
items: India's Struggle for Independence presents the No-changer versus Pro-changer debate as
a disagreement over method after the suspension of mass struggle.
No-changers defended Gandhian constructive work as preparation for future struggle and as a way to keep Congress rooted among the people.
Swarajists argued that entering legislatures would prevent political passivity, expose colonial reforms and wreck dyarchy from within.

groups.heading: ADVANCED DEBATE
items: Their 1923 successes gave them a platform, but obstruction had limits because executive power remained colonial and C.R.
Das's death in 1925 weakened leadership.
The HRA aimed at an armed overthrow of colonial rule and a republican India; Kakori was intended to obtain funds and publicise revolutionary courage.
Bhagat Singh's generation reorganised the movement as the HSRA, adding a clearer socialist and anti-imperialist vocabulary.

groups.heading: LEGACY / NUANCE
items: The Assembly Bomb was deliberately non-lethal and symbolic, meant "to make the deaf hear" and use the courtroom as a platform.
CAUTION: Bhagat Singh's writings, including "Why I am an Atheist," show a
shift from heroic individual action toward ideological, rationalist and socialist politics.
Swaraj Party was founded on 1 January 1923 ; C.R. Das was president and Motilal Nehru secretary.
